findings.description: The bucket has no ACL restricting access (comment indicates it is public) and lacks any public access block configuration, exposing customer data to the internet.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so data stored in this bucket is not encrypted at rest by default.
The bucket has no versioning block configured, allowing accidental or malicious overwrite/deletion of objects without recovery.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so access to sensitive customer data would not be recorded for audit purposes.

A customer master data file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded into the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, exposing potentially sensitive customer records to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving it unencrypted at rest.
No versioning block is configured, risking permanent loss or tampering of financial records without recovery capability.
No logging block is configured, so access to sensitive financial data is not audited.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving operational data unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, preventing audit of access to operations data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving data science datasets unencrypted at rest.
